source.title: STAPLE: Static Sparse Upcycling of Pretrained Checkpoints via Embedding Modules
source.authors: Ranajoy Sadhukhan; E. Hong; Sheng Cao; Ze-Chun Liu; Shuo-Wei Jin; Sha Li; Chang-Long Yu; Xin Liu; Qin Lu; Zhen-Yu Shi; Priyanka Nigam; Bei-Di Chen

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream scores while scaling static-memory capacity in pretrained models, a new setting for the downstream-predictability version of the claim. It does not test the original pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as background but does not test their loss laws. Rows below capture its own downstream benchmark results across static-memory capacities and the reported embedding-removal ablation; comparisons to other methods are not recorded unless they directly report a capacity-related result.
record.test_reason: STAPLE is a method paper. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as motivation and reports its own upcycling recipe's downstream scores. The 'capacity sweep' has only three configurations of one method: L=4, L=12, and low-rank L=12, on two different axes. There is no fit, no loss measurement and no test of whether scores track scale or pretraining loss predictably. The 1B-to-7B comparison changes the backbone and the budget, so it is not a scale test. The removal ablation measures reliance on co-adapted memory, not scaling. The capacity trend is recorded under fits_no_version, not as a test of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that STAPLE is a sample-efficient way to add static sparse capacity to pretrained checkpoints. They report that average downstream score rises with static capacity, that gains persist on OLMo-2 7B, and that it beats STEM, Engram-style and MoE upcycling baselines at near-dense throughput. They fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: The study upcycles pretrained checkpoints by adding token-indexed static-memory modules and evaluates downstream benchmarks; it does not fit held-out-loss scaling laws or optimize parameter/token splits under fixed compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream averages differ with the number of augmented layers and embedding rank; results also differ across the 1B and 7B backbones and task metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: On OLMo-2 1B upcycling, the ten-task average rises with total parametric capacity added as token-indexed static memory: 44.39 at 1.07B dense, 44.97 at 1.74B (L=12, r=512), 45.10 at 4.36B (L=4) and 45.59 at 10.94B (L=12). Roughly a tenfold increase in parameters gives +1.2 points, with non-uniform per-task changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In sparse upcycling, downstream average improves slowly and monotonically with added static-memory parameters at a fixed token budget.

record.problems: The capacity comparison is limited to a small set of static-memory configurations and downstream benchmarks. The study does not estimate a predictive scaling curve or report uncertainty for these score comparisons. The 7B experiment uses a reduced training budget, and its proposed explanation for the modest MMLU gain is not isolated.
record.rows_left_out: Individual per-task Table 2 scores and the per-task score changes in the table-removal ablation are not separately enumerated here; the average rows and reported 7B task count capture the capacity trend and its non-uniformity. Table 2 contains the per-task values; Section 4.1 and Figure 5a report the removal results. Other architecture, warmup, throughput, and energy comparisons do not measure the claim versions recorded here.

untested.parts: No held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fixed-parameter shape comparison of loss.
No power-law form in any other regime. Continued training is not fitted.
No relation of downstream scores to scale or loss beyond three own-method configurations, and no predictive fit.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels should be dropped. The rows are the method's own variant-versus-baseline comparisons, and the removal ablation is not a scale manipulation. The total-capacity values from Fig 1b (1.074B, 1.741B, 4.362B, 10.939B) should be added to the size_stated fields of the T2 rows if the capacity trend is kept under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; bottleneck conditions; power-law fits.
Prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count, including depth and width effects on loss.
Power-law behavior in other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Does not relate downstream results to pretraining loss or establish a predictive scaling law; tests a limited static-memory capacity sweep and downstream benchmark scores.
No scaling-law exponents, fit choices, or compute-optimal allocations are estimated or compared.

rows.subject: Baseline (OLMo-2 1B)
rows.operation_detail: Dense continued-training baseline for the static-memory capacity sweep
rows.measure: Average score across ten downstream benchmarks
rows.note: Reference score for the capacity variants.
rows.check: Dense continued-training control (44.39) for the method's own comparison. It does not measure downstream predictability with scale.

rows.subject: STAPLE (L=4)
rows.operation_detail: Scale static-memory capacity by augmenting four layers
rows.measure: Average score across ten downstream benchmarks
rows.note: Average is higher than the dense baseline.
rows.check: Own-method variant versus a baseline. One point is not a predictive scaling relation. Fig 1b gives total capacity as 4.362B; the row says 'not stated'.

rows.subject: STAPLE (L=12)
rows.operation_detail: Scale static-memory capacity by augmenting twelve layers
rows.measure: Average score across ten downstream benchmarks
rows.note: Average rises from 45.10 at L=4 to 45.59 at L=12.
rows.check: Own-method variant. Total capacity is 10.939B per Fig 1b, not recorded in the row. Of the 10 tasks, 3 (ARC-C, WinoG, MATH) fall below the baseline.

rows.subject: STAPLE (L=12, r=512)
rows.operation_detail: Scale static-memory capacity using a low-rank embedding table
rows.measure: Average score across ten downstream benchmarks
rows.note: Above the dense baseline but below full-width STAPLE-12L.
rows.check: Low-rank variant with 1.741B total parameters (Fig 1b), on a different capacity axis from L. Own-method comparison only.

rows.subject: Baseline (OLMo-2 7B)
rows.operation_detail: Dense continued-training baseline for the 7B comparison

conditions.value: approximately 30B warmup tokens and 70B mid-training tokens

rows.measure: Average score across ten downstream benchmarks
rows.note: Reference score for the 7B STAPLE comparison.
rows.check: 7B dense control trained on a reduced budget (30B+70B tokens). Not comparable to the 1B rows as a scale point.

rows.subject: STAPLE (L=16)
rows.operation_detail: Add static-memory tables to the first 16 decoder layers

conditions.value: approximately 30B warmup tokens and 70B mid-training tokens

rows.measure: Average score across ten downstream benchmarks
rows.note: The text also reports improvement on 9 of 10 evaluated tasks.
rows.check: Method-versus-baseline gain on the 7B backbone. It does not measure how performance changes with scale.

rows.subject: STAPLE (L=16)
rows.operation_detail: Add static-memory tables to the first 16 decoder layers

conditions.value: approximately 30B warmup tokens and 70B mid-training tokens

rows.measure: Number of evaluated tasks improved over baseline
rows.note: The text does not identify in this statement which task did not improve.
rows.check: Count of tasks improved by the method over the baseline. 'Partial' against V6 is not meaningful, since this is a method comparison.

rows.subject: STAPLE-12L checkpoint
rows.note: Reference condition for the table-removal ablation.
rows.check: Reference value that duplicates T2-L12-avg. A removal ablation is not a scaling measurement.

rows.subject: STAPLE-12L checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Remove the last four embedding tables without retraining
rows.note: Removing capacity lowers the downstream average.
rows.check: Removing tables from a co-adapted checkpoint without retraining tests reliance on the memory, not scale. 'Reversed' is the wrong state.

rows.subject: STAPLE-12L checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Remove the last eight embedding tables without retraining
rows.note: Removing capacity lowers the downstream average.
rows.check: Same as ABL-4: this is a reliance ablation, not scaling. 'Reversed' is wrong.

rows.subject: STAPLE-12L checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Remove all twelve embedding tables without retraining
rows.note: The authors note that remaining weights had co-adapted with static memory, so this is not equivalent to the original dense seed.
rows.check: Same as ABL-4. The authors note the ablated model is not equivalent to the dense seed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Average downstream scores in the OLMo-2 1B static-memory capacity sweep and the OLMo-2 7B comparison
reader_labels.reason: The ten-task average rises from 44.39 for dense OLMo-2 1B to 45.10 and 45.59 for STAPLE L=4 and L=12, and the 7B average rises from 57.11 to 58.01 (T2-base-avg, T2-L4-avg, T2-L12-avg, T7-base-avg, T7-L16-avg).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Task-level performance and low-rank static memory
reader_labels.reason: The mean trend is not uniform across tasks, 9 of 10 7B tasks improve, and low-rank STAPLE has a lower average than full-width L=12; removing tables also lowers the trained checkpoint's average (T2-r512-avg, T7-L16-count, ABL-4-avg, ABL-8-avg, ABL-12-avg).
